item.title: Rent for two-bed apartment rose by 13pc in Leitrim in 2025
item.description: Rent for a two-bedroom apartment in Leitrim rose by nearly 13 per cent last year. Daft.ie found the average monthly bill was €1,225 in the last three months of 2025 - up 12.9 per cent on 2024. It rose by almost 6 per cent in Longford, to €1,315. Advertisement But they dropped by nearly 8 per cent in Roscommon, to €1,263. Local auctioneer Ivan Connaughton says a lack of homes is driving up prices: Advertisement

item.title: 'We remember our families still in Ukraine, who continue to suffer' - Ukrainian tells anniversary Mass in Longford
item.description: Ukrainian refugees in Longford have prayed for peace and justice, on the fourth anniversary of the Russian invasion. A special Mass was held in St Mel's Cathedral last night. Up to 140,000 Ukrainians have lost their lives in the war over the past four years. Advertisement Ukrainian refugees are living in 405 family homes in Co Longford. item.title: N5 bypass between Ballinagare and Tibohine to open next month
item.description: It's expected a section of the new N5 Ballaghaderreen to Scramogue bypass will be open in the coming weeks. Roscommon County Council chief executive Shane Tiernan confirmed the news at yesterday's council meeting. It's hoped a 7km section of the road from Ballinagare/Frenchpark to Tibohine will be opened by the end of March. item.title: Crowds fill Carrick streets for Fair Trade Parade
item.description: Crowds filled the streets of Carrick-on-Shannon this morning for the annual Fair Trade Parade. Community groups, local businesses and schoolchildren turned out in force to celebrate the town’s commitment to ethical trade. The parade is part of what's called 'Fairtrade Fairbruary'. Advertisement It is hoped to encourage people to choose Fairtrade products and support farmers and workers worldwide. item.title: Man dies in county Sligo crash
item.description: A man has died in a crash in county Sligo. The two-vehicle collision occurred in the Rusheen area of Riverstown. Gardaí and emergency services were alerted to the incident, involving a lorry and a motorcycle, at approximately 9:20am. Advertisement The motorcyclist, a man in his 50s, was pronounced dead at the scene. item.title: Concern raised about damaged telecom wires in Co. Roscommon
item.description: Concerns have been raised about hanging and damaged telecommunications cables across parts of County Roscommon following last winter's storms. While broadband services were restored quickly, it's believed the physical infrastructure has not been fully repaired in many rural areas. Areas like Fairymount, Lisacul and routes towards Castlerea have seen long stretches of cable remain hanging along roadsides and across farm entrances. item.title: Bishop Doran condemns the 'evil' of the Ukraine war, on 4th anniversary
item.description: The Bishop of Achonry and Elphin is condemning the 'evil' of the Ukraine war, on the fourth anniversary of Russia's invasion. Kevin Doran is expressing his deep support for Ukrainian people who are living in his diocese. He says they'd much prefer to be at home with their own people. item.title: County Leitrim native elected as new DCU Student Union President
item.description: A county Leitrim woman has been elected as President of the Dublin City University Students Union for the 2026/2027 academic year. Katherine McBride, who is studying Economics, Politics and Law, is a native of Dromahair. Ms McBride topped the poll, with 1,551 first preference votes and was elected on the first count. She is the first female president of the student representative body since 2019. Shane Murphy from Lecarrow in Roscommon is the current President. Advertisement

item.title: Shock and sadness in local community following crash
item.description: There's said to be widespread shock and sadness in a county Sligo community close to the border with Roscommon and Leitrim. That's after a motorcyclist died after a crash involving a lorry. It happened at Rusheen in Riverstown at around 20 past nine this morning.
